summary: Two segmented date fields sharing one calendar, returning an inclusive { start, end } of YYYY-MM-DD strings.
useWhen: the user picks a period — a report window, a stay, a filter over time
the range commonly crosses a month boundary, so both ends need to be visible at once
there are conventional periods worth offering as shortcuts: last 7 days, month to date, year to date

useInstead.when: the choice is really a named period and the exact dates are incidental
useInstead.why: if 'Last 30 days' is the answer rather than a shortcut to one, a calendar is scaffolding around a list of five options

useInstead.when: one end is open — everything before, or everything since
useInstead.why: with the open end expressed as minValue or maxValue. This component has no half-open value on purpose; see antiPatterns

sm.use: dense forms, table filters, dashboard toolbars

guarantees: both fields sit in one labelled group; each announces its own name, so 'Start Date' and 'End Date' are heard without a visible sublabel, and each editable segment is its own tab stop as it is in DatePicker
the dash between them is aria-hidden — the fields have already said what they are, and a spoken dash adds nothing
the calendar is modal: focus enters the grid, the page behind is hidden from assistive tech, Escape closes and focus returns
a range cannot be made to run backwards, in either direction of selection, and cannot be dragged across an unavailable day
preset rows are buttons in a labelled group carrying aria-pressed, so 'which shortcut is active' is answerable without seeing the tint
the selected preset is marked by weight as well as by background, so it does not rely on colour alone
range endpoints and the band between them keep their fill under forced-colors, where background-color is otherwise discarded
the rail stacks above the grids below 32rem rather than being hidden, because shortcuts matter most on the device where dragging across two months is worst
requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered
`presetsLabel` wording if the default is wrong for the context — it names the whole shortcut group
preset labels that say what period they select, since the label is the button's entire accessible name

antiPatterns.dont: expecting an Apply button, or adding one
antiPatterns.why: the value commits when the second end lands and the calendar closes. A draft model makes Escape and an outside click silently discard a selection the user watched themselves make, and there is no way to tell those gestures apart from 'I am done'. Clear exists because clearing has no other affordance

antiPatterns.dont: passing a range with only one end, or reading one back
antiPatterns.why: a start with no end is a state the calendar passes through between the two clicks, never a value the caller is handed. 'Everything after March' and 'March to today' are different questions and a null end cannot say which was meant

antiPatterns.dont: writing a relative preset as a literal object
antiPatterns.why: `value: { start: '…', end: '…' }` is evaluated once, when the module is first imported. 'Last 7 days' is then seven days before whenever the tab was opened. Pass a function; it is re-run each time the calendar opens

antiPatterns.dont: composing this out of two DatePickers
antiPatterns.why: two independent pickers cannot stop the end preceding the start, cannot draw the band between the ends, and make the user reconcile two calendars from memory

antiPatterns.dont: setting visibleMonths to 1 for a filter that usually spans weeks
antiPatterns.why: the user then pages back and forth to see both ends of their own selection. One month is for ranges that genuinely sit inside one
the range is closed. A stay of 3 nights from the 1st ends on the 4th in checkout terms and on the 3rd here; convert at your boundary, not in the picker

label.expects: what the period is for — 'Reporting period', not 'Dates'

presets.expects: conventional periods for this screen, longest-lived first: today, last 7 days, month to date, year to date

description.expects: helper text under the fields; replaced by `errorMessage` when `isInvalid`

errorMessage.expects: what is wrong with the range and what would be right, shown only when `isInvalid`
